LESSON: WATER ITS RESOURCES

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Environment and
Topic 1.2: Water its resources

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Water its resources. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: why water is stored water at home and in the home and school at homes and school. school?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain why clean water is important
2. list ways water is used at home and school
3. describe simple ways to conserve water in Kenya
4. practise safe water habits

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WATER ITS RESOURCES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Water its resources helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT WATER
We use water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and farming.
Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.
Unsafe water can cause disease — store drinking water in clean covered containers.

PART 1: Explain why clean water is important

What this means
In this part you learn to explain why clean water is important. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain why clean water is important.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Water its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain why clean water is important. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: List ways water is used at home and school

What this means
In this part you learn to list ways water is used at home and school. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: list ways water is used at home and school.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Water its resources matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can list ways water is used at home and school. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe simple ways to conserve water in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to describe simple ways to conserve water in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe simple ways to conserve water in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Water its resources this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe simple ways to conserve water in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Practise safe water habits

What this means
In this part you learn to practise safe water habits. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise safe water habits.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Water its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise safe water habits. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Water its resources is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Water its resources” around your school. (skill: explain why clean water is important)

Example 2: Say why Water its resources matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: list ways water is used at home and school)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Water its resources this week. (skill: describe simple ways to conserve water in Kenya)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Water its resources” around your school. (skill: practise safe water habits)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Water its resources to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain why clean water is important.
3. Practise this skill: list ways water is used at home and school.
4. Practise this skill: describe simple ways to conserve water in Kenya.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Water its resources from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Water its resources: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Water its resources?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why water is stored water at home and in the home and school at homes and school. school?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Water its resources means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain why clean water is important.
5. Be able to: list ways water is used at home and school.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
